newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gold, silver end lower poor demand.
newsitem.headline: Indian gold, silver end lower poor demand.

text.p: ** Standard gold 24 carats closes 10 rupees lower at 4,770 rupees per 10 grammes on poor demand after opening steady at 4,780 rupees.
** Gold biscuits (116.50 grammes) close 200 rupees lower at 55,800 rupees per piece. They opened steady at 56,000 rupees per piece.
** Silver.999 ends 60 rupees lower at 6,780 rupees per kg after wiping out part of its losses in early trade. It opened 90 rupees lower at 6,750 rupees per kg on increased arrivals.
Standard gold 24 carats closed 10 rupees lower at 4,470 rupees on poor demand. It opened steady at 4,780 rupees per 10 grammes.
"There's a temporary slump in demand. But I expect prices to move upwards within a week," said Bombay Bullion Association president Makhan Lal Damani.
Dealers said imports of gold and silver under special import licences (SILs) had been higher than before.
Special import licences are issued against export earnings of traders and are traded openly.

"The premium for acquiring these SILs has fallen to around 10.65 percent fro 14 percent in the last few days because of their easy availablity following a recent liberal export-import policy," said bullion dealer Bhayabhai Sanghavi.
"The undertone is weak in anticipation of higher supplies," said Sanghavi said.
He said many Indian expatriates and local traders had booked gold imports taking advantage of a recent downslide in its international prices.
Gold biscuits (116.50 grammes) closed 200 rupees lower at 55,800 rupees after opening steady at 56.000 rupees per piece.
Silver .999 closed 60 rupees lower after wiping out part of its losses in early trade. It opened 90 rupees down at 6,750 rupees per kg on increased arrivals. (Conversion $1=35.76 rupees)
